input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds only Customer, is a true no-hire ("hire, or employ"), covers every Vendor employee rather than personnel involved in the Services, runs 24 months post-term, and expressly overrides any general-advertising or unsolicited-application carve-out ("regardless of how the employee applies"). That fails the fallback (mutual, involved personnel only, 12 months, with carve-outs and no no-hire) on every material term and sits in walk-away territory because it is a no-hire covering all Vendor personnel. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment and is free to hire anyone responding to general recruitment. We therefore propose deleting 12.4 to reach the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), and offer the narrow mutual 12-month fallback in the comment.

proposal.summary: Delete the one-way 24-month no-hire on Customer in Section 12.4
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a one-way no-hire that covers every Vendor employee for 24 months and expressly captures people who apply through general recruitment, and it contradicts Section 12.3, so we have deleted it. If Vendor needs protection, we can accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends, with carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches.
